headline: Indian minister Jitendra Singh said India has reached 1,000 kilometres of quantum-secure communication in three years, half of its 2,000-kilometre target for eight years.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a new statement from 10 Oct, but it is a minister's own claim with no technical detail or independent check.
importance_line: India says it is ahead of schedule on quantum-secure communication links, which would matter to government and security users, but the claim is the minister's own and the report does not say which technology or links it covers.
summary: Kashmir News Service reports that Jitendra Singh, India's Minister of State for Science and Technology, told a PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry meeting in New Delhi on 10 Oct 2026 that India has covered 1,000 kilometres with quantum-secure communication in three years, half of the 2,000 kilometres it set out to reach in eight, and credited the National Quantum Mission. The report does not say which technology or links the figure covers, and he used the speech mainly to urge industry to join research earlier.
